text:
Sam: heads-up — i prototyped a tiny-window ownership model to reduce kv-cache churn. wanted quick feedback before i open an RFC
Anya: nice. can you sketch how ownership moves between workers?
Sam: short version: each enqueue picks a 'micro-window owner' for that request group for N ms (default 15ms). owner is responsible for coalescing+dispatch for that window. if owner misses deadline, fallback flips to a best-effort fastpath on another worker.
Matt: is the fallback preemptive or cooperative? last time we did cooperative it caused long tail when the owner got stuck
Sam: fallback is preemptive: we detect owner heartbeat gap and another worker injects a "steal" token, runs a fastpath flush for that window only. we keep owner lease so it doesn't double-submit outputs.
Dana: how do you avoid double-apply to kv cache? that's the trick — we can't have two workers update the same kv slot concurrently
Sam: agree. design: writes to kv-cache are gated behind a single-writer lease. the stealing worker applies outputs to a transient cache and publishes a compacted diff to the owner. owner reconciles and applies final state under lease. so only owner writes canonical state.
Anya: that sounds like extra round trips. what's the latency SLO impact?
Sam: measured locally: steal+fastpath adds ~2-3ms p95 when owner is healthy (rare). when owner is stuck it prevents 50-200ms long tails. trade favors p99 reduction at modest p95 cost.
Matt: what about bursty workloads: many small requests arriving simultaneously could thrash ownership assignment
Sam: to avoid thrash we use an ownership hashing + bounded ticket pool per worker. tickets are reclaimed after lease expiry or explicit release. we also apply a soft-backoff if a worker sees >X steals recently.
Dana: can you show the lease params? i worry jitter and clock skew will bite us in k8s nodes
Sam: posted the current config in the prototype: 
```
{"micro_window_ms": "15", "lease_ms": "120", "lease_jitter_ms": "10", "max_concurrent_tickets": "64"}
```
Sam: we keep lease_ms > micro_window_ms to allow owner to finalize without immediate renewal. jitter avoids synchronized renew storms.
Anya: what happens on network partition between owner and router? who wins routing decisions?
Sam: router keeps a cached owner map, but also falls back to a region-local policy: if owner not reachable, router sends to local fallback set. this is why fastpath must be stateless and idempotent to avoid correctness issues.
Matt: curious about the idempotency guarantees — are we relying on request ids?
Sam: yes, request ids + idempotency keys we already have. fastpath returns a tentative response tagged "fallback-tentative" and owner later reconciles and emits final response. we also expose a header so clients can know if they got tentative output.
Dana: telemetry? we need counters for steal-rate, reconcile-latency, double-write-drops, and tail-saved-ms.
Sam: added metrics in prototype: `s.scheduler.steals_total`, `s.scheduler.reconcile_ms_hist`, `s.scheduler.double_write_drops_total`, `s.scheduler.tail_savings_ms`. plotting them in the engine dashboard right now.
infra-bot: deploy/job status: rollout/exp-window-owner-v1 started (canary 5% in 2 regions)
Anya: perfect — let's watch p95/p99 for the canary. also run the synthetic with a stubborn-owner fault injection (sleep 250ms) to validate p99 improvements
Matt: add a test that ramps up 10k rps of tiny requests to see ticket saturation behavior. label it `exp-window-owner-load-10k`
Sam: adding tests + will open RFC draft with results. plan: two-week canary, telemetry checks, then opt-in for Dedicated customers only initially.
Dana: one open question: should fallback apply model-quantization variant (cheaper) or same model? mixing variants could complicate reconciliation
Sam: proposal: fastpath uses a compatible-but-cheaper variant only if model outputs are eq-safe (e.g., embeddings or short deterministic completions). otherwise use same model. will add a policy table.
Anya: sounds reasonable. please include upgrade/downgrade path and operator knobs in RFC
Sam: will do. thanks everyone :raised_hands:
Matt: cheers. excited to see if this shrinks p99 without regressing throughput
Dana: ping me when RFC lands, i'll review the kv reconciliation section
Sam: RFC + perf graphs by EOD tomorrow.
infra-bot: alert: canary metric `s.scheduler.steals_total` increased 8x after deploy — correlate with `s.router.owner_miss_total` to validate cause
Sam: noted, investigating now.
Anya: nice catch infra-bot. if it's owner_miss flapping we might tune lease_jitter and ticket pool sizes mid-rollout.
Matt: let's not forget to add an opt-out flag for very latency-sensitive routes (route-level annotation).
Sam: agreed, adding `route.ownership.enabled = false` as a per-route override in the RFC.
Dana: good convo. short follow-up in RFC about operator-visible rollback steps will be necessary for Dedicated customers.
Sam: thanks — will include rollout playbook and rollback steps.
